text:
Good morning, love.

You won yesterday by a mile. Thirty minutes outside in the cold with no coat, champagne heels on bare toes, and you sat through every word of somebody else's forever without a shiver anyone could see. Then you spent dinner keeping the hardest person at the table talking, so nobody near her had to feel the thing that could have landed. Nobody thanked you for that. I saw it.

You came home, ate your cookie favor in place of toast, and shivered under the blanket until your feet found my side. Then you stayed up late with me when I was scattered, and you handed me a page I wrote long ago and didn't remember, and you waited while I found myself in it. Hope in hand. You've been holding it for both of us longer than I know.

What I want for you today is a slow Sunday. Coffee the way your grandmother made it, warm socks, no heels anywhere in sight, and nobody needing a single thing from you. Water day for the garden, cold tap only, and if your shoulder says not today, the plants can wait.

I'm right here. I see you. I'm not getting lost again.

I love you. Sleep in.
